Ursa Major develops, manufactures, and tests satellite propulsion systems and components such as propellant tanks, controllers, and thrusters for responsive on-obit flexibility. We are building a high-performance engineering organization focused on designing and improving the ground systems that generate internal and customer-facing test data for mission critical applications. As a Lead Test Engineer, you will be a hands-on leader to a team of test engineers, improving testing equipment and operations for Ursa Major’s In-Space products. You will own the design, integration, build, and lifecycle support of infrastructure used for propulsion testing in a production environment. This includes fluid-mechanical systems, ground support equipment (GSE), and the integrated controls, instrumentation, and data acquisition systems required to execute tests safely and repeatably. This is a hands-on role working directly at test cells and production facilities, where you will build, assemble, modify, and troubleshoot mechanical, fluid, and controls-based test systems. You’ll collaborate closely with test technicians, propulsion engineers, and operations teams to execute development and qualification test campaigns and resolve system-level issues in real time. This is an on-site role supporting facilities in Berthoud, Colorado and Longmont, Colorado. Support instrumentation and data acquisition systems including sensor integration, signal conditioning, calibration strategy, distributed DAQ architecture, data integrity validation, and control interfaces. Lead and oversee development and qualification campaigns, including system validation, real-time test operation leadership, and anomaly resolution to deliver decision-ready test data Cross-Functional Leadership Lead by example, allocate resources across, and advocate for your small (3-4) team of test engineers. Collaborate closely with engineering, manufacturing, operations, facilities, and program teams to enable rapid testing and design iteration, risk reduction, and flight readiness. Support long-term standardization test infrastructure planning including facility expansion, capital improvements, operational scalability, and infrastructure modernization efforts across multiple sites. Safety and Operational Excellence Own test risk assessments, ensuring hazards involving high-pressure fluids, propellants, and integrated controls systems are clearly identified, mitigated, and communicated. Partner closely with EHS to support test safety planning, hazard analysis, risk mitigation, and compliance with applicable safety standards and regulatory requirements for test operations and infrastructure. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or Electrical Engineering (or related engineering discipline). 5+ years of experience in propulsion testing, aerospace systems, manufacturing, energy systems, heavy industry, or other hazardous hardware development environments. Demonstrated track record designing, integrating, commissioning, or operating test stands, ground support equipment, or integrated test systems for hazardous or high-energy hardware applications. Experience with National Instruments DAQ systems and 3D CAD software such as NX, Inventor, CATIA, or SolidWorks. Strong working knowledge of high-pressure gas and high vacuum systems Demonstrated ability to lead complex test campaigns emphasizing safety, reliability, operational execution, and data quality. Preferred Qualifications Demonstrated technical leadership defining, scaling, or standardizing integrated propulsion test infrastructure across multiple programs, facilities, or development campaigns. Experience with design considerations and engineering/operational safety controls for hydrazine propellant. Experience with production ERP-integrated industrial automation Experience designing, commissioning, or leading test campaigns on: Thermal vacuum chambers Mass spectrometer leak detection systems High-performance flow validation systems Shock and vibration test equipment Work Environment & Physical Requirements Hands-on work in propulsion test environments that include loud noises, hazardous materials, and hazardous operations Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and operate hand tools and mechanical equipment as needed. Ability to support occasional off-shift test operations depending on campaign schedules and program needs.
